title: A nonzero map into a locally constant etale sheaf has locally nonzero germs
statement: Let X be any scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], N,F abelian sheaves on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and ψ:N→F a nonzero morphism. Assume the underlying set sheaf of F is locally constant [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Then there exist a nonempty etale X-scheme U and a section s∈N(U) such that for every algebraically closed field Ω in the scheme universe, every geometric point t:Spec Ω→X and every lift v:Spec Ω→U of t, the germ [ψ_U(s)]_(U,v) in F_t [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is nonzero.

source.place: First proof step: nonzero germ, local trivialization, and refinement to distinct constant sections

proof.text: For a nonzero morphism ψ:N→F, geometric stalk exactness and conservativity imply joint faithfulness: if all stalk maps were zero, the image sheaf would have all stalks zero, hence would be zero, forcing ψ=0. Choose a stalk element with nonzero image and represent it by a section s on a pointed etale neighbourhood.

Use the covering of the underlying set sheaf of F to choose a trivializing member V containing the image of the marked point. The point lifts to V by Mathlib Scheme.pointSmallEtaleFiberObjToPreimage_surjective. Refine by the fibre product with V. Pointed neighbourhoods lying over V are cofinal (each neighbourhood is refined by its fibre product with V), so the stalk and its nonzero image germ are unchanged.

Identify the restriction of the underlying set sheaf with the constant set sheaf M. Its stalk is M: sheafification preserves geometric stalks of sets, and the constant presheaf has stalk M because the opposite category of pointed neighbourhoods is nonempty and connected. The image germ and the zero germ correspond to distinct m,z∈M. Equality of elements in a filtered colimit holds after a common refinement. Refine the section so that its image is the constant section m and the zero section is the constant section z.

Call the refined neighbourhood U. It is nonempty because it carries the retained marked point. At any geometric point t of X and lift v to U, cofinality identifies the germ with that on the trivializing member. The constant-sheaf stalk computation identifies image and zero with m and z, still distinct. Thus the image germ is nonzero for every Ω,t,v as asserted. No compatibility with group addition of the set-sheaf trivialization is needed.
